U.S. senators are trying to force artificial intelligence companies to disclose how their models work and what safeguards they have to protect the public against them, Semafor reported.

The AI transparency bill, which was released on Thursday, comes from a bipartisan group of senators, including Chris Coons (D-Del.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Katie Britt (R-Ala.), and James Lankford (R-Okla.), the news outlet added. If enacted, the bill would ask the Federal Trade Commission to enforce these disclosures for AI companies.
